topSignals.title: FuelCell Energy reports Q3 FY2026 miss but lands its first data-center Capacity Reservation Agreement — 75 MW in Texas.
topSignals.text: Revenue fell 29% YoY to $33M; a $24.5M gross loss (including $17M of inventory write-downs and firm-purchase-commitment charges tied to the Fit Energy Phase 0 agreement) drove an adjusted loss of $0.64/share, missing the $0.53 estimate by ~21%. Backlog rose 4.1% YoY to $1.3B and Awarded Capacity Backlog grew by $2.4B on Fit Energy's option for up to 350 additional MW. The new deal — six 12.5 MW FuelCell Energy Block systems for an unnamed major data-center operator, upfront reservation payment, definitive agreements still pending — is FCEL's first standalone data-center contract distinct from the Fit Energy relationship. Stock fell ~13% on the day as the loss overshadowed the deal. GlobeNewswire | SEC 8-K | 24/7 Wall St.

topSignals.title: MISO files its Large Load Interconnection Reliability Requirements Tariff with FERC (Aug 28), closing the overdue flag from yesterday's digest.
topSignals.text: The filing (docket EL26-70-000) responds to FERC's June 18 show-cause order and sets technical standards — visibility/modeling data, real-time and day-ahead load forecasting — for any facility over 50 MW connecting to MISO's grid; it does not itself decide the case. MISO's and transmission owners' full show-cause response to FERC remains due Nov 16, 2026. Directly relevant to how fast AI-load interconnection queues clear versus the on-site SOFC alternative. Utility Dive | FERC RM26-4

topSignals.title: Project Jupiter: Sept 2 response deadline to the NM Supreme Court stay has passed with no ruling found yet; Oracle reaffirms commitment.
topSignals.text: The stay (issued Aug 23–24) still pauses both the NMED air-quality permit hearing for Bloom's 2.45 GW fuel-cell system and an emergency well-water authorization at the Oracle/OpenAI Doña Ana County campus; neither underlying legal challenge has been decided on the merits, and the stay does not itself halt construction. Oracle said publicly it remains committed to developing the project "responsibly." No new court action identified as of this digest — carries into a new week. UPR | Source NM

items.text: Elcogen (priority): Quiet for a fifth straight day. No news beyond the already-logged Aug 24 Paris MoU; background unchanged (E3000 G2 platform rollout, 360 MW Tallinn factory, Casale P2X MoU, JNK India MoU).

Topsoe (priority): Quiet. No news beyond the already-logged Aug 27 H1 2026 results and the May 2026 SOEC-pathway/Herning-hibernation decision. The ABB/Fluor alliance for a standardized next-generation SOEC factory concept (targeting Chesterfield, Virginia, by 2028) is background context, not new — first surfaced pre-hibernation.
Other players: No new stack/cell announcements found today from Bloom, Ceres Power, Sunfire, SolydEra, Mitsubishi Power, Kyocera, Aisin, or Convion.
FuelCell Energy first standalone data-center Capacity Reservation Agreement (Texas, 75 MW): See Top Signal #1.
Project Jupiter (Oracle/OpenAI, NM): See Top Signal #3 — court response deadline passed, no ruling yet.

Standing pipeline unchanged: Bloom-AEP 1 GW ($2.65B), Bloom-Brookfield $5B partnership, Bloom-Nebius $2.6B, Bloom-Equinix >100 MW/19 sites, FCEL-Fit Energy up to 380 MW (+$2.4B awarded-capacity option), Ceres-Centrica UK/Europe multi-GW pipeline, FCEL-SDCL up to 450 MW.
MISO large-load tariff filed with FERC (Aug 28): See Top Signal #2 — resolves the "overdue" flag carried since Sept 1.
Project Jupiter (NM): Court response deadline passed — see Top Signal #3.

Rolls-Royce SMR UK GDA: Design Acceptance Confirmation is contingent on completing Step 3 ("detailed assessment"), self-targeted for August 2026; no confirmation of issuance found — now carries into a third week unresolved. Not SOFC-specific but relevant as a competing on-site baseload timeline benchmark.

Germany EnEfG: Unchanged — the June 24 draft act to accelerate EU Energy Efficiency Directive transposition (which could soften the PUE ≤1.2/waste-heat-reuse targets already in the LCOE model) is still pending a Bundestag/Bundesrat floor vote this autumn; no schedule found yet.
Texas ERCOT audit, US ITC 45V/48E, Virginia data-center legislation: unchanged.

FuelCell Energy (FCEL): Q3 FY2026 — see Top Signal #1. Revenue $33M (-29% YoY), gross loss $24.5M, adjusted EPS -$0.64 (miss vs -$0.53 est.), backlog $1.3B (+4.1% YoY), Awarded Capacity Backlog +$2.4B, annualized production rate ~37 MW (target 100 MW by October 2026). Stock -13% on the day.

Bloom Energy (BE): Last reliably confirmed level is the $200–206 range as of Sept 1 (-3.5% intraday on a securities-suit legal-notice reminder); a same-day search today returned a materially different price/market-cap that doesn't reconcile with Bloom's known share count or 52-week high (~$351) and is being treated as bad data rather than reported — worth a manual check if you need today's exact print. Lead-plaintiff deadline reminder: Sept 28, 2026. Next scheduled catalyst: 10-Q on Sept 11.
Topsoe: Nothing beyond the already-logged Aug 27 H1 2026 results.
Ceres Power (CWR.L): No new pricing/news beyond the already-logged Aug 26 RFC Power £10M Series A spin-out (37% retained stake).

lcoe.text: The August 2026 EIA STEO (the current, most defensible vintage) confirms Henry Hub averaging ~$3.91/MMBtu in Q3 2026 — resolves the reconciliation flagged Sept 1–2 between the October-2025-vintage $3.70/4Q and the model's current $4.00–4.30/MMBtu assumption. This is now the number to reconcile against directly rather than the older STEO print; consider whether the model's gas-price assumption should move down slightly toward ~$3.90–4.00/MMBtu for near-term (2026) scenarios. EIA STEO PDF

Pending carry-forward, unchanged: Rolls-Royce SMR GDA completion (self-set target passed, still unconfirmed), Germany EnEfG Bundestag/Bundesrat vote (autumn 2026), Texas ERCOT audit (~Dec 10, 2026), Bloom 10-Q (Sept 11), Ceres H1 2026 results (September, date unconfirmed), Bloom securities-fraud lead-plaintiff deadline (Sept 28), Bloom Q3 2026 earnings (Oct 27), FCEL production ramp to 100 MW annualized (October 2026).
